test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Feb, 2026 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. But in college Ralph's goals were still hazy and undefined.
A. Though he continued to take classes here and there in the sciences and in the Department of Business, he also took some lower-division classes in history and philosophy and English.
B. He first thought he wanted to be a doctor, or a lawyer, and he took pre-medical courses and courses in history of jurisprudence and business-law before he decided he had neither the emotional detachment necessary for medicine, nor the ability for sustained reading and memorization in the Corpus Iuris Civilis, as well as the more modern texts on property and inheritance.
C. But it never came.
D. He continually felt he was on the brink of some kind of momentous discovery about himself.
S2. It was during this time, his lowest ebb, as he jokingly referred back to it later, that he believed he almost became an alcoholic; he was in a fraternity and he used to get drunk every night.</span
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph focuses on Ralph's unclear goals during college and his struggles with self-discovery.
 
• **Sentence B is the first in the sequence** because it introduces Ralph's initial aspirations and his realization that he lacked the qualities needed for certain professions:
 
 
• "He first thought he wanted to be a doctor, or a lawyer, and he took pre-medical courses and courses in history of jurisprudence and business-law before he decided he had neither the emotional detachment necessary for medicine, nor the ability for sustained reading and memorization in the Corpus Iuris Civilis, as well as the more modern texts on property and inheritance."
 
 
 
• **Sentence A follows** as it describes his continued indecisiveness and exploration of various subjects:
 
 
• "Though he continued to take classes here and there in the sciences and in the Department of Business, he also took some lower-division classes in history and philosophy and English."
 
 
 
• **Sentence D is the third sentence** as it reflects Ralph's internal struggle and his feeling of being on the verge of a significant realization about himself:
 
 
• "He continually felt he was on the brink of some kind of momentous discovery about himself."
 
 
 
• **Sentence C is the last** as it concludes that the anticipated discovery never happened:
 
 
• "But it never came."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **BADC**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"He first thought he wanted to be a doctor, or a lawyer, and he took pre-medical courses and courses in history of jurisprudence and business-law before he decided he had neither the emotional detachment necessary for medicine, nor the ability for sustained reading and memorization in the Corpus Iuris Civilis, as well as the more modern texts on property and inheritance. Though he continued to take classes here and there in the sciences and in the Department of Business, he also took some lower-division classes in history and philosophy and English. He continually felt he was on the brink of some kind of momentous discovery about himself. But it never came."</div
